data.title: Diaper (napkin) dermatitis — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Diaper (napkin) dermatitis** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. Define diaper dermatitis.**
- Inflammatory eruption in the area covered by a diaper; most commonly irritant contact dermatitis in infants (peak 9–12 months); also in incontinent adults

**Q2. Pathogenesis of irritant napkin dermatitis.**
- Occlusion and over-hydration of skin → friction damage
- Urine urea broken down by faecal urease → ammonia raises pH → activates faecal lipases and proteases that damage the barrier
- Diarrhoea, antibiotics, infrequent changing worsen it; Candida commonly colonises after 72 h

**Q3. Classify diaper dermatoses / differentials (PYQ).**
- Irritant (convex surfaces affected, folds spared — 'W' pattern)
- Candidal (folds involved, beefy red with satellite pustules)
- Infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis (folds, salmon-coloured, greasy scale, scalp involved)
- Psoriasis (napkin psoriasis — sharply demarcated, may spread to trunk)
- Jacquet's erosive dermatitis (punched-out erosions — severe irritant)
- Granuloma gluteale infantum (purple nodules after potent steroids)
- Allergic contact dermatitis (dyes, rubber, fragrance — waistband/ thighs)
- Others: bullous impetigo, perianal streptococcal dermatitis, acrodermatitis enteropathica (zinc deficiency — periorificial erosions, diarrhoea, alopecia), Langerhans cell histiocytosis (petechial, eroded, in folds — biopsy), congenital syphilis, scabies, herpes, Kawasaki (perineal desquamation)

**Q4. Distinguish irritant from candidal napkin dermatitis.**
- Irritant: convexities (buttocks, genitals, thighs) affected; flexures spared; shiny glazed erythema
- Candidal: flexures involved, bright red with satellite papules/pustules and peripheral scale; KOH positive

**Q5. Management.**
- ABCDE: Air (diaper-free time), Barrier (zinc oxide, petrolatum, dimethicone at each change), Cleansing (gentle water, avoid wipes with fragrance/alcohol), Diapers (super-absorbent disposable, frequent changes — every 2–3 h, immediately after stools), Education
- Mild steroid (1% hydrocortisone) for 3–5 days if inflamed — never potent steroids under the diaper (occlusion → atrophy, granuloma gluteale)
- Candidal: topical clotrimazole/miconazole/nystatin; treat oral thrush
- Bacterial: topical mupirocin/oral antibiotics

**Q6. What is granuloma gluteale infantum?**
- Purplish-red oval nodules on buttocks/groin in infants with napkin dermatitis treated with potent topical steroids (or Candida); benign, resolves over months after stopping steroid

**Q7. What is Jacquet's erosive dermatitis?**
- Severe irritant form with punched-out erosions or ulcers with raised edges, papules in the napkin area; also in adults with incontinence/urostomy

**Q8. Why test zinc in persistent diaper rash?**
- Acrodermatitis enteropathica (SLC39A4 mutation or acquired — premature/breastfed by low-zinc mothers) presents with perioral and perianal eroded, crusted dermatitis, diarrhoea, alopecia, irritability; low serum zinc/alkaline phosphatase; rapid response to zinc 1–3 mg/kg/day

**Q9. When should you biopsy?**
- Non-response to standard care, petechiae, erosions, papules in folds with hepatosplenomegaly (LCH), nodules — to exclude LCH, psoriasis, granuloma gluteale

**Q10. Describe the histopathology of eczema by stage (PYQ).**
- Acute: marked spongiosis with intraepidermal vesicles, papillary oedema, perivascular lymphocytes ± eosinophils
- Subacute: spongiosis + parakeratosis + acanthosis, crusts
- Chronic: compact hyperkeratosis, irregular/ psoriasiform acanthosis, hypergranulosis, minimal spongiosis, vertical collagen in papillae (lichenification)

**Q11. Describe napkin psoriasis.**
- Well-demarcated bright red glazed plaques in napkin area including folds, often with psoriasiform lesions elsewhere (scalp, umbilicus, trunk); family history; may herald childhood psoriasis; treat with mild steroids, calcipotriol, tacrolimus

**Q12. Langerhans cell histiocytosis in the napkin area — clues.**
- Persistent erosive/ petechial papules in folds (unlike irritant), scalp seborrhoeic-like scaling, purpura, hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, bone lesions, diabetes insipidus; biopsy — CD1a+, CD207 (langerin)+ histiocytes; refer oncology

**Q13. Allergic contact dermatitis in diaper area.**
- Less common; allergens — disperse dyes in diapers (blue/ pink), rubber additives (elastic bands — 'lucky Luke' pattern on outer buttocks/ thighs), fragrances in wipes (methylisothiazolinone), sorbitan sesquioleate; patch test in persistent cases; switch to dye-free diapers

**Q14. Perianal streptococcal dermatitis.**
- Bright red, well-demarcated perianal erythema with pain on defecation, fissures, blood-streaked stools in children 6 months–10 years (group A strep); rapid strep test/ swab; treat with oral penicillin/ amoxicillin 10 days + topical mupirocin

**Q15. Barrier products — composition and mechanism.**
- Zinc oxide (protective, mildly antiseptic), petrolatum (occlusive), dimethicone (silicone barrier), lanolin, titanium dioxide; apply thick layer at each change; avoid talc (inhalation risk) and boric acid

**Q16. Classify topical corticosteroids by potency (WHO/ British).**
- Super-potent (class I): clobetasol propionate 0.05%, halobetasol, betamethasone dipropionate in optimised vehicle
- Potent: betamethasone dipropionate/ valerate 0.1%, mometasone furoate 0.1%, fluticasone 0.05%, fluocinolone 0.025%, halcinonide
- Moderate: clobetasone butyrate 0.05%, triamcinolone 0.1%, desonide, hydrocortisone butyrate
- Mild: hydrocortisone 1–2.5%
- Ointments more potent than creams of same molecule; avoid potent on face, flexures, genitals, infants

## Quick spotter facts
- Folds spared — irritant; folds involved + satellites — Candida
- Potent steroid under nappy → granuloma gluteale infantum

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Neonatal and paediatric dermatoses). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
